h: Each Soul and Tribe Within the Sacred Whole

p: שְׂאוּ אֶת רֹאשׁ כָּל עֲדַת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
"Take a census of the entire assembly of the Bnei Yisrael
Now here it lists five expressions:
first, "according to their families, by their fathers' house";
fourth, "from twenty years old and upward";
fifth, "everyone who goes out to the army in Yisrael."
And likewise all these expressions are mentioned
in the count of each and every tribe.
And likewise in the pasuk "And they declared their pedigrees" etc.
four of the expressions are mentioned:
"And they declared their pedigrees according to their families, by their fathers' house";
third, "from twenty years old and upward";
except "all who go out to the army,"
וְנִרְאֶה שֶׁהוּא עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁכָּתַב הָרַמְבַּ״ן זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה
And it seems that this follows what the Ramban, of blessed memory, wrote:
the meaning of "everyone who goes out to the army" is
all those who go out to assemble in the congregation,
כִּי הַנְּעָרִים לֹא יַקְהִילוּ בְּתוֹךְ הָעֵדָה
for the youths are not assembled within the congregation.
And therefore, since in the pasuk "And they declared their pedigrees"
it begins, "and they assembled the entire congregation" (Bamidbar 1:18),
לֹא הוּצְרַךְ לִכְתּוֹב כָּל יוֹצֵא צָבָא
it did not need to write "everyone who goes out to the army,"
since those assembled in the congregation
are the ones who go out to the army.
Now we must understand the matter of the five expressions
that are mentioned in the command,
and afterward in the fulfillment of the mitzvah, "And they declared their pedigrees,"
וְאַחַר כָּךְ בְּמִסְפַּר כָּל שֵׁבֶט וָשֵׁבֶט
and afterward in the count of each and every tribe.
And the matter is that the count was
to know the number of the hosts of the Torah
and the hosts of the Mishkan,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (רֵישׁ פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ)
as is written in the holy Zohar (beginning of this parsha, III 117a)
"in the Wilderness of Sinai, in the Tent of Meeting":
one is for the Torah and one is for the Mishkan.
Now our Sages, of blessed memory, said
that the nefesh is attained from the time of formation,
when one becomes thirteen years old,
and the neshamah when one becomes twenty years old.
וְהוּא דְּנֵר ה׳ נִשְׁמַת אָדָם (מִשְׁלֵי כ, כז)
And this is: "The lamp of Hashem is the soul of man" (Mishlei 20:27);
"Your word is a lamp for my feet
and a light for my path" (Tehillim 119:105).
the words of Torah that give him light.
וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר מִבֶּן עֶשְׂרִים שָׁנָה וָמַעְלָה
And about this it says, "from twenty years old and upward,"
corresponding to the hosts of the Torah,
which one attains when he is twenty,
"Everyone who goes out to the army in Yisrael"
corresponds to the hosts of the Mishkan;
for regarding the donations to the Mishkan it is written,
וַיַּקְהֵל מֹשֶׁה אֶת כָּל עֲדַת וְגוֹ׳ (שְׁמוֹת לה, א)
"And Moshe assembled the entire congregation" etc. (Shemos 35:1),
שֶׁהוּא כָּל יוֹצְאֵי צָבָא הַנִּקְהָלִים בָּעֵדָה
which means all who go out to the army, those assembled in the congregation,
as the Ramban, of blessed memory, wrote.
And it says, "every male, by their heads":
that is, to give the ransom for the soul,
And it says, "by the number of names,"
עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁכָּתַב הָרַמְבַּ״ן זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה
according to what the Ramban, of blessed memory, wrote
on the pasuk "And they declared their pedigrees according to their families" etc.:
and witnesses to the presumption of their birth," etc.;
וְהִקְשָׁה הָרַמְבַּ״ן זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה עַל זֶה
and the Ramban, of blessed memory, raised a difficulty on this
and wrote that nothing was needed
מַה שֶּׁהֵבִיא שִׁקְלוֹ לִפְנֵי מֹשֶׁה כּוּלֵּי
bringing his shekel before Moshe, etc.,
said, "I, so-and-so, was born to so-and-so
And it is possible to reconcile Rashi's explanation:
that they nevertheless needed to bring
witnesses to the presumption of their birth,
so that no one should come to contest them,
as happened with the son of the Mitzri,
who wished to pitch his tent in his mother's tribe;
even though there was only one such case,
and Hashem Yisbarach testified about them,
"The tribes of Yah, a testimony for Yisrael"
מִכָּל מָקוֹם הוּצְרְכוּ לְהָבִיא סִפְרֵי יִחוּסֵיהֶם
nevertheless they needed to bring their books of lineage
and witnesses to the presumption of their birth,
to remove any slander and challenge.
And this is what it says: "according to their families, by their fathers' house."
And it says, "by the number of names":
הוּזְכַּר כָּל אֶחָד שְׁמוֹ וְשֵׁם אָבִיו
each one's name and his father's name was mentioned
as the Ramban, of blessed memory, wrote,
and this was so that they would pray for them;
וּכְעֵין מַה שֶּׁכָּתַב הָרַמְבַּ״ן זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה
similar to what the Ramban, of blessed memory, wrote
בַּפָּסוּק וַיִּהְיוּ כָּל פְּקוּדֵי בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְגוֹ׳
on the pasuk "And all those counted of the Bnei Yisrael were" etc. (Bamidbar 1:45):
that they be counted before Moshe and Aharon,
so that they would set their eyes upon them for good
ה׳ אֱלֹהֵי אֲבוֹתֵיכֶם יוֹסֵף עֲלֵיכֶם (דְּבָרִים א, יא)
"May Hashem, the God of your fathers, add to you" (Devarim 1:11),
And this is the matter of the five expressions
that are mentioned each time, as stated.
And this is why the mitzvah was
לִהְיוֹת הַמִּפְקָד עַל יְדֵי מֹשֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן וְהַנְּשִׂיאִים
that the census be carried out through Moshe and Aharon and the Nesi'im.
For Moshe was for the matter of the hosts of the Torah:
שֶׁכָּל נֶפֶשׁ יֵשׁ לוֹ חֵלֶק בַּתּוֹרָה
that every soul has a portion in the Torah,
וְהוּא אוֹת אוֹ חֵלֶק מֵאוֹת בְּסֵפֶר תּוֹרָה
and it is a letter or part of a letter in a Sefer Torah,
such that if the letter is missing,
in the Sefer Torah, it becomes invalid.
And Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
הָיָה שׁוֹרֶשׁ כָּל הַשִּׁשִּׁים רִבּוֹא נְפָשׁוֹת
was the root of all the six hundred thousand souls,
which are the letters of the Torah;
and the Torah is called by his name,
And Aharon was for the matter of the hosts of the Mishkan,
for Aharon is the root of the avodah,
and this corresponds to the expression
"everyone who goes out to the army in Yisrael," as stated.
"according to their families, by their fathers' house";
לִישָּׂא כָּל אֶחָד אוֹת שֶׁל שִׁבְטוֹ
for each to carry the banner of his tribe,
that is, how it is bound at the root to Hashem Yisbarach,
"'In the beginning' — for the sake of Yisrael,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב הָרְמַ״ע בְּסֵפֶר עֲשָׂרָה מַאֲמָרוֹת
as the Rema of Fano wrote in Sefer Asarah Maamaros:
the soul of the father is the mazal of the son.
And the Nasi likewise indicates this,
and it is stated in Sefer Yetzirah (6:2):
"The heart in the soul is like a king at war";
for the king is like the heart,
"Above all that you guard, guard your heart,
for from it are the sources of life";
and likewise the king is the life-force of the world,
and the Nasi is the life-force of the tribe.
of those who possess the middos of the ten Sefiros,
the Nesi'im of Yisrael were counted
as corresponding to the middah of Keser.
That is, each Nasi clarified his tribe,
that they are bound to the Mazla,
which is Atika, the middah of Keser;
and Keser Elyon is Keser Malchus.
And corresponding to this is the expression
"according to their families, by their fathers' house."

p: why, after the census of each tribe is mentioned,
וַיִּהְיוּ כָּל פְּקוּדֵי בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְגוֹ׳ (בְּמִדְבַּר א, מה)
"And all those counted of the Bnei Yisrael were" etc. (Bamidbar 1:45),
וַיִּהְיוּ כָּל הַפְּקוּדִים וְגוֹ׳ (שָׁם א, מו)
So why did the Torah write the sum total?
by adding together the counts of the tribes?
And likewise the count is repeated afterward
in the parsha of the banners,
when each tribe was reckoned with its Nasi,
and likewise the count of each banner;
and afterward there is repeated yet again
the total count of all the banners.
וּבַתּוֹרָה אֵין אַף אוֹת אַחַת מְיוּתָּר
And in the Torah not even one letter is superfluous,
all the more so entire parshiyos.
But in truth we find something similar
in the parsha of the offerings of the Nesi'im,
where with each Nasi it repeats "his offering" etc.,
even though every Nasi's offering was identical,
"And likewise the Nasi of such-and-such a tribe offered."
וְכֵן כְּתִיב אַחַר כָּךְ פָּרָשָׁה שְׁלֵימָה
And likewise afterward an entire parsha is written,
זֹאת חֲנוּכַּת הַמִּזְבֵּחַ וְגוֹ׳ (בְּמִדְבַּר ז, פד)
"This was the dedication of the Altar" etc. (Bamidbar 7:84),
the sum total of the offerings.
וְנִרְאֶה שֶׁזֶּה הָיָה קָשֶׁה לְהַמִּדְרָשׁ רַבָּה
And it seems that this was difficult for the Midrash Rabbah,
different allusions for each and every tribe.
That is, although the offering was identical,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם הָיָה לְכָל אֶחָד מֵהַנְּשִׂיאִים
nevertheless each of the Nesi'im had
a particular intention in his offering.
And likewise afterward, on the sum total
of all the offerings of the Nesi'im,
That is, when all the numbers of the offerings
there was in this a different intent.
the Ramban, of blessed memory, asked
and why it was written in the Torah,
and he wrote: "Perhaps to make His kindness known to them,
that with seventy souls they went down to Mitzrayim,
and behold they are like the sand of the sea."
after all, in Mitzrayim they were many more,
for only one in five went up,
אוֹ אֶחָד מֵחֲמֵשׁ מֵאוֹת (תַּנְחוּמָא בְּשַׁלַּח א)
or one in five hundred (Tanchuma, Beshalach 1),
and so then there were many more,
But the main intent of the count
was for the raising of their heads,
עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (אָבוֹת ד, ג)
in the manner of what they said (Avos 4:3):
אֵין לְךָ אָדָם שֶׁאֵין לוֹ שָׁעָה כּוּלֵּי
"There is no person who does not have his hour," etc.
That is, every one of Yisrael,
at that hour and in that matter,
is the greatest of all Yisrael,
and so too his fellow at another hour.
And this is because every one of Yisrael
has a portion in the Torah,
a letter or part of a letter,
such that when that letter is missing,
And this was the matter of the hosts of the Torah
how each and every soul is unique
in its holiness and in its Torah,
among the hosts of the Torah.
And this is why the expressions are repeated,
for they allude to different matters in each tribe.
and the twelve permutations of the Name Havayah
And Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him,
"each according to his blessing he blessed them."
וְזֶה הָעִנְיָן שֶׁנִּפְקַד כָּל שֵׁבֶט בִּפְרָט
And this is why each tribe was counted individually,
each one among the hosts of the Torah,
to know the hosts of the Mishkan.
And likewise all five expressions are mentioned
for the purpose we have said;
and this is repeated with each tribe,
שֶׁבְּכָל שֵׁבֶט הָיָה מְכֻוָּון מְיוּחָד בָּזֶה
for with each tribe there was a particular intent in this.
And afterward the count was written all together,
for in the combination of the entire count of the tribes
there was in them a different holiness and secret,
known to Moshe and to Aharon.
And afterward, in the parsha of the banners,
when they were counted together with the Nesi'im,
אָז נִשְׁנָה מִנְיַן כָּל שֵׁבֶט וָשֵׁבֶט
then the number of each and every tribe was repeated
That is, it was in his power
to clarify for each member of his tribe
how he is bound to the Mazla,
and this is "by their fathers' house," as stated.
וְאָז גַּם כֵּן נִשְׁנָה כְּלַל הַמִּסְפָּר
And then too the total count
for it has a different secret and intent
in the number of the souls of the camp of the banner.
And afterward the count was repeated
when they are counted together with their Nesi'im;
for in this there is a particular intent,
beyond when they were counted previously
And this is the root of the entire parsha.
And on Shabbos every one of Yisrael
merits an additional nefesh and ruach,
and they also merit a neshamah,
each one according to his level,
וְכֵן כָּל אֶחָד לְפִי הַהֲכָנָה שֶׁלּוֹ
And likewise each one, according to his preparation,
that is, how he is bound at the root
to the Mazla, which is Atika:
"'In the beginning' — for the sake of Yisrael,
and this is the task of the Nesi'im.
And likewise it is the time to repair all the past,
"If your sins be like the years
these years that come in order
from the six days of Creation
they shall be made white as snow" (Shabbos 89b).
That is, when it becomes clear
that in the first utterance, where darkness is mentioned,
it was in order that there be
light that comes forth from within darkness,
in which are mentioned all the matters referred to
in the expressions "according to their families" etc.,
And every Shabbos has in it
some of the holiness of the parsha read on it;
it is the time to merit all that has been said.
